video_title: Tatum Brown BEEF | Did Boston Undervalue Jaylen Brown?

quotes.speaker: Jay King
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla's perspective on the Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum dynamic
quotes.excerpt: Jason is with us now, Jason is the one we're going to focus on, and Jason is our guy.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: I was reading your latest piece up on The Athletic and you guys talked to Joe Mazzulla about the sniping that's been going on back and forth. I want to read some of these Mazzulla quotes to you guys. Quote: 'These two guys, they were together for nine seasons and they had great, great moments together. And at the end of the day, nobody is perfect. We can all get better. We all did great things. We all did things that we want to be better at. So I think it's more just focusing on the greatness that those two were able to achieve and the fact that they're both great people.' You're a Mazzulla-ologist, Jay. What are we supposed to glean from that?

text_blocks.speaker: Jay King
text_blocks.text: I think the more interesting part was what he said next, which was that they're both very different people, they act differently, they operate differently. And then he said basically, as much as I appreciate what Jaylen did for us, Jason is with us now, Jason is the one we're going to focus on, and Jason is our guy. And I think that's where he stands on it. He's like, you know what, they can do whatever they want to do together, but at this point, I'm the coach of the Boston Celtics. Jaylen's not on my team anymore, and I love the guy, I respect him, I think he's a great person, but also, to me, that was kind of like flip the middle finger, and we're moving on with our guy Jason.

quotes.speaker: Jay King
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's post-game comments and his relationship with Jayson Tatum
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Brown gives his press conference after the game that they played against Milwaukee and what stuck out.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Jaylen Brown gives his press conference after the game that they played against Milwaukee and what stuck out to me was the 'lamb chops' line. The 'lamb chops' line was stupid because it's just whatever and it made me laugh. But what stuck out to me was like, 'He's got great PR.' Oh, that was the one that was the direct shot at Jason. Because that's how different they are. Like, he's the one who is raw, who says what he means, who is unfiltered, has his own shoe company, isn't signed with Nike or anybody else. And then Jason has always been buttoned up, has always done things by the book.

text_blocks.speaker: Jay King
text_blocks.text: And I don't think it's fake or anything. That's just how he operates. But that's what Jaylen Brown is saying, though. Exactly. And he's saying, he's saying basically like, go have fun dealing with his canned answers and the stuff that his publicist told him to tell you. And so, yeah, I thought that was like, I don't know if it was intentional, probably wasn't intentional, but like, it was kind of cutting, cutting Jaylen where, where it would probably hurt after, he thought he proved himself last year as capable of being the guy for Boston. Obviously they traded him right after that, and now, now there are a lot of raw emotions, and so it's, it's funny because there were three years in a row when the Celtics were just robots, that no drama, and now, now it's, it's drama. There's drama, man.

quotes.speaker: Jay King
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum's involvement in Celtics front office roster decisions
quotes.excerpt: Jayson Tatum has not been one of those stars who wants to have a hand in everything.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Does it ring true to you, the idea that Jayson Tatum was caught way off guard when Jaylen Brown got traded? I found out just like the rest of you guys. I had no idea anything like this was in the works. Does that have even a morsel of truth to it to you?

text_blocks.speaker: Jay King
text_blocks.text: By the time Jaylen got traded, it was already in the media that he was being shopped. It was not clear that he was definitely getting traded, but I think everybody knew at that point there was a real chance that Jaylen got traded. That said, Jayson has not been one of those stars who wants to have a hand in everything in an organization. In the past, they traded Javonte Green, his closest friend in Boston. He has said before how he does not really want to be involved in stuff like that and just trusts Brad. I do believe he was not fully advocating for Jaylen to go.

quotes.speaker: Jay King
quotes.summary_phrase: Historical friction regarding Jaylen Brown's valuation by the Celtics
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen probably just never felt appropriately valued by Boston. I'm talking about never.
quotes.quote: It goes back a long way to where Jaylen probably just never felt appropriately valued by Boston. I'm talking about never. So his second year, he starts on a team that goes to the Eastern Conference Finals Game 7, loses to LeBron in Game 7, and he played great that whole run. He comes back the next year, Jayson Tatum is starting, and he gets moved to the bench. He was probably like, what the hell? Why am I the one who gets moved to the bench? I think there were just a bunch of times when the way he saw himself was not the way the team saw him. In 2022, they go to the Finals, then they have talks about trading for Kevin Durant. Those become public. So he has got to be like, what the hell? That summer, Kevin Durant and Jayson Tatum were working out together. I think along the way there was a lot of stuff that Jaylen moved past.
